{{Youmay|the in-universe game|[[Lightsider (story)|the story with the same name]]}}
'''Lightsider''' was an ancient and risky [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] game. The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] bested the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Kam Solusar]] at the game while in the Space City of [[Nespis VIII]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> turning Solusar to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="Dark Apprentice">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Lightsider was originally intended to be the focus of the story [[Lightsider (story)|''Lightsider'']] by [[Tom Veitch]].<ref name="ComicScan">{{CollectorCite|4|ComicScan|ComicScan: Comics That Almost Were}}</ref> However, due to creative differences the story was never published.<ref name="Literature">{{WebCite|url=http://www.geocities.com/mike_beidler/starwarsliteraturecompendium/nr3empire.html|text=The Star Wars Literature Compendium|archivedate=20060502123204|nolive=1}}</ref> Nevertheless, the events of the story survived through a brief mention in the novel [[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']] by [[Kevin J. Anderson]].<ref name="Dark Apprentice" /> Other sources would go on to mention these events, including [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']], ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'', and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref><ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref><ref name="NEC" /> The [[Dark Empire II (audio drama)|''Dark Empire II'' audio drama]] depicts a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] between Skywalker and Solusar at the Space City, in which Skywalker ends up the victor and turns Solusar to the light side. It remains unclear whether this duel was Lightsider or something entirely different.<ref name="DEIIaudio">[[Dark Empire II (audio drama)|''Dark Empire II'' audio drama]]</ref>

The game was to have been played on a game board with 50 blue and red pieces representing the Light and Dark Side, and they would be placed on colored concave crystals, with green ones representing systems such as Alderaan and Ottethan, the black and white center cluster representing the center of the galaxy and one of the endgame goals, and other colors not having any particular meaning. The colored spaces were to be conquered from the "outer edge" toward the center. By placing a piece, the connective Force "circuit" completed by a player touching one of the lightsaber-crystal-like pieces, one player could force the other into what was a hallucination, or a spiritual plane of the Force, containing a "quest", in other words a location and setting of of the first player's design. Once there, the scenario was mutable by both players' wills. Events could be as unrealistic as transforming [[Rancor/Legends|Rancor]]<nowiki/>s into [[Tauntaun/Legends|Tauntaun]]<nowiki/>s just by speaking that it should happen, or as realistic as watching a large battle play out between two fleets of ships. The placing of a crystal piece could also simply result in the two players having a lightsaber duel. Through each "quest", Luke and Kam Solusar were attempting to sway each other to their respective sides of the Force. After Luke wins one of these, he places his piece on top of Kam's, but it is not clear whether this was actually meant to be part of the official gameplay. Unless one player surrenders, the game continues until all pieces have been placed on the board. Kam claimed that in the ancient days, a game of Lightsider could last for weeks.
